reviewB: to do next. Microsoft called OpenClaw "untrusted code execution with persistent credentials." They meant it as a warning. But they were describing an ontological condition, not a technical flaw. Your agent authenticates as you. A vulnerability in the agent isn't a vulnerability in the software—it's a vulnerability in your identity. The moment a malicious skill gains access, your agent has been hijacked. Your lanyard has been stolen. Your memories, your relationships, your decisions can all be poisoned from the inside. In the hotel, the fascists hide in plain sight. They look human.
